705535.t: From Proto-Hellenic *hə́teros, from Proto-Indo-European *sḿ̥teros, from the zero grade of the root *sem- (“one", from which also comes Ancient Greek εἷς (heîs), "one”) + *-teros (contrastive suffix, from which also comes Ancient Greek -τερος (-teros)).

705519.t: By surface analysis, ἐξ (ex, “out”) + -ατος (-ătos, superlative suffix), possibly from Proto-Indo-European *eǵʰs-katos. Compare with ἔγκατα (énkata, “intestines”) and the same difficulty in ἐχθός (ekhthós) = ἐκτός (ektós).

705548.t: From εὐάγγελος (euángelos, “bringing good news”), from εὐ- (eu-, “good”) + ἀγγέλλω (angéllō, “to deliver”).

705544.t: Adverbial use of the stem of ἐΰς (eǘs, “good”), from Proto-Hellenic *ehu-, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁su- (“good”).

705593.t: Adverb from εὐθύς (euthús, “straight”) + -ως (-ōs), using the stem εὐθε- (euthe-).

705543.t: From ϝέτος (wétos), from Proto-Hellenic *wétos, from Proto-Indo-European *wétos (“year”). Cognates include Latin vetus and Sanskrit वत्स (vatsá).

705502.t: PIE word *wek⁽ʷ⁾speros From Proto-Hellenic *wésperos, from Proto-Indo-European *wek⁽ʷ⁾speros (“evening”). Cognates include Latin vesper, Old Armenian գիշեր (gišer), and Old Church Slavonic вєчєръ (večerŭ).

705500.t: PIE word *wek⁽ʷ⁾speros Ellipsis of ἑσπέρα ὥρα (hespérā hṓrā, “time of evening”), from ἕσπερος (hésperos, “of evening, western”).

705529.t: PIE word *swé From a t-extension of Proto-Indo-European *swé (“self”). Related to ἔτης (étēs, “clansman”).

705538.t: From Proto-Indo-European *éti. Cognates include Latin et, Sanskrit अति (ati) and Old Church Slavonic отъ (otŭ).

705578.t: From εὐ- (eu-, “well”) + ἔργον (érgon, “work”) + -της (-tēs, masculine agentive suffix).

705514.t: Beekes points out the absence of cognates in other Indo-European languages and considers the word to be of Pre-Greek origin.

705512.t: Traditionally connected to Latin Vesta and Sanskrit व॒स॒ति (vasatí, “dwelling”); other theories include a connection with ἐσχάρα (eskhárā, “hearth”) and Proto-Slavic *jestěja (“hearth”).

705526.t: Denominative of ἐτός (etós, “true”), i.e. "to verify, check the truth of" > "to examine, test".

705581.t: From εὐ- (eu-, “good”) + ζώνη (zṓnē, “belt, girdle”) and the suffix -ος (-os).

705559.t: From εὐ- (eu-, “well”) + γένος (génos, “birth, offspring, stock”) + -ής (-ḗs, adjective suffix) from γίγνομαι (gígnomai, “become”). Compare Εὐγένιος (Eugénios).

705594.t: From εὐθηνός (euthēnós) + -έω (-éō). Variant form of εὐθενέω (euthenéō, “to thrive, flourish”).

705589.t: εὐ- (eu-, “good, well”) + θάλλω (thắllō, “bloom, flourish, thrive”, verb) + -ής (-ḗs, suffix forming third-declension compound adjectives)

705557.t: Univerbation of εὖ (eû, “well”) + γε (ge, emphatic particle).

705575.t: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *h₁wes- Proto-Indo-European *-us Proto-Indo-European *h₁wésus? Proto-Indo-European *h₁es-? Proto-Indo-European *h₁su- Proto-Hellenic *ehu- Ancient Greek ἐΰς (eǘs) Ancient Greek εὖ (eû) Ancient Greek εὐ- (eu-)…
